title: Agent reliability observation row
description: One row per executed arm. Field order is not fixed; semantics are. Rows are JSONL: one JSON object per line, no trailing comma, LF line endings, final line carries a newline.

case_id.description: Stable identifier of the case. Version suffix is part of the identifier, so a case can change shape without impersonating an older one.

criterion_digest.description: Digest of the criterion set the row was judged against. Each executor computes it over its own copy. Cross-executor computation is not permitted.

trigger_condition.description: Written-out condition that makes the arm fail. A sample file is not a trigger condition.

failing_behavior.description: What the failure looks like from the outside, including the exit code.

expected_verdict.description: What the arm is required to produce. NOT_EXERCISED, NOT_APPLICABLE and UNKNOWN are observation outcomes and never appear here.

expected_reason_code.description: Closed set, single value per class. The set is versioned, individual codes are not.

must_fail_arm_ref.description: Pointer to the arm that carries the injection.

injector_id.description: Issuer of the injection. The injector issuer and the criterion implementer must be disjoint. An arm whose injector is the implementer is void.

control_direction.description: Role of the arm in the batch. Never average across roles.

channel.description: Channel the arm travels on. Part of the unique key, recorded with multiset semantics.

comparison_basis.description: How a comparison between two products is taken. Field level comparison needs a declared value domain, which a noop-versus-injected pair cannot guarantee.

volatile_fields_policy.description: Versioned exclusion list for volatile fields. An undeclared exclusion turns the arm into a coin flip.

examples.trigger_condition: cut sample inside a multibyte sequence, tail missing a continuation byte
examples.failing_behavior: lenient decoder returns valid-looking short output, exit code 0
